default.title: comma four setup
default.summary: Install your comma four in five steps.

steps.title: Remove the rearview mirror cover trim
body: Removal method varies by car. The plastic often needs a firm tug on Hondas; Toyotas often need a slide outward.
Use a vehicle-specific installation video to check how the cover releases.

steps.title: Connect car harness into the camera
body: Unplug the existing LKAS camera connector and plug it into the harness.
Connect the other end of the harness back into the LKAS camera.
Find a spot for the harness box so the trim can still fit over it. Peel off the adhesive backing and attach the box in place.

steps.title: Place mount high and centered on the windshield
body: Clean the mounting area with the included alcohol wipe and let it dry.
Leave enough room for the cable when the device is mounted, and make sure you can see the screen from a seated position.
Center the mount horizontally so the device can properly center in the lane.
Peel off the mount's tape cover. Press firmly in the center, then the edges. Make sure no bubbles form.

steps.title: Plug in OBD-C and mount the device
body: Plug the OBD-C cable into the harness box. Make sure the cable is fully seated.
Plug the OBD-C cable into the comma four. Make sure the cable is all the way in.
Slide the device onto the mount until it is fully seated.

steps.title: Reinstall the rearview mirror cover trim
body: Make sure the car harness fully fits inside the trim.
Generally, it is best to have the OBD-C cable come out of the top.

Audi A3 2014-19.title: Audi A3
Audi A3 2014-19.summary: Your VW J533 connector connects at the gateway. Follow the vehicle-specific steps below.

steps.title: Access the gateway under the dashboard
body: Remove the lower dashboard trim in the driver's footwell to reach the gateway.
Identify the gateway and release its connector locking mechanism before unplugging it.

steps.title: Connect the harness at the gateway
body: Unplug the vehicle connector at the gateway and plug it into the matching end of your car harness.
Plug the other end of the harness back into the gateway. Make sure the connector locks are fully engaged.
Secure the harness box where the trim can fit back in place without pinching any cables.

steps.title: Place mount high and centered on the windshield
body: Clean the mounting area with the included alcohol wipe and let it dry.
Leave enough room for the cable when the device is mounted, and make sure you can see the screen from a seated position.
Center the mount horizontally so the device can properly center in the lane.
Peel off the mount's tape cover. Press firmly in the center, then the edges. Make sure no bubbles form.

steps.title: Plug in OBD-C and mount the device
body: Route the long OBD-C cable from the harness box to the windshield. Keep it clear of pedals, moving parts, and airbag deployment paths.
Plug the OBD-C cable into the harness box. Make sure the cable is fully seated.
Plug the OBD-C cable into the comma four. Make sure the cable is all the way in.
Slide the device onto the mount until it is fully seated.

steps.title: Secure the cable and reinstall the trim
body: Secure excess cable so it cannot move into pedals, seat rails, or other moving parts. Keep airbag deployment paths clear.
Check that the harness and cable fit behind the panels, then reinstall the trim you removed.

body: Release the plastic cover behind the rearview mirror to reach the driver-assistance camera.
Release the cover's clips carefully; leave the camera attached to the windshield.

steps.title: Connect car harness into the camera
body: Unplug the existing LKAS camera connector and plug it into the harness.
Connect the other end of the harness back into the LKAS camera.
Find a spot for the harness box so the trim can still fit over it. Peel off the adhesive backing and attach the box in place.

steps.title: Place mount high and centered on the windshield
body: Clean the mounting area with the included alcohol wipe and let it dry.
Leave enough room for the cable when the device is mounted, and make sure you can see the screen from a seated position.
Center the mount horizontally so the device can properly center in the lane.
Peel off the mount's tape cover. Press firmly in the center, then the edges. Make sure no bubbles form.

steps.title: Plug in OBD-C and mount the device
body: Plug the OBD-C cable into the harness box. Make sure the cable is fully seated.
Plug the OBD-C cable into the comma four. Make sure the cable is all the way in.
Slide the device onto the mount until it is fully seated.

steps.title: Reinstall the rearview mirror cover trim
body: Make sure the car harness fully fits inside the trim.
Generally, it is best to have the OBD-C cable come out of the top.

body: Slide off the cover around the camera behind the rearview mirror to expose its connector.
Keep the camera attached to the windshield while fitting the harness.

steps.title: Connect car harness into the camera
body: Unplug the existing LKAS camera connector and plug it into the harness.
Connect the other end of the harness back into the LKAS camera.
Find a spot for the harness box so the trim can still fit over it. Peel off the adhesive backing and attach the box in place.

steps.title: Place mount high and centered on the windshield
body: Clean the mounting area with the included alcohol wipe and let it dry.
Leave enough room for the cable when the device is mounted, and make sure you can see the screen from a seated position.
Center the mount horizontally so the device can properly center in the lane.
Peel off the mount's tape cover. Press firmly in the center, then the edges. Make sure no bubbles form.

steps.title: Plug in OBD-C and mount the device
body: Plug the OBD-C cable into the harness box. Make sure the cable is fully seated.
Plug the OBD-C cable into the comma four. Make sure the cable is all the way in.
Slide the device onto the mount until it is fully seated.

steps.title: Reinstall the rearview mirror cover trim
body: Make sure the car harness fully fits inside the trim.
Generally, it is best to have the OBD-C cable come out of the top.

steps.title: Place mount high and centered on the windshield
body: Clean the mounting area with the included alcohol wipe and let it dry.

Plug the OBD-C cable into the comma four. Make sure the cable is all the way in.
Slide the device onto the mount until it is fully seated.

steps.title: Secure the cable and reinstall the trim
body: Secure excess cable so it cannot move into pedals, seat rails, or other moving parts. Keep airbag deployment paths clear.

Škoda Fabia 2022-23.summary: Your VW J533 connector connects at the gateway. Follow the vehicle-specific steps below.

steps.title: Access the gateway under the dashboard
body: Remove the lower dashboard trim in the driver's footwell to reach the gateway.
Identify the gateway and release its connector locking mechanism before unplugging it.

steps.title: Connect the harness at the gateway
body: Unplug the vehicle connector at the gateway and plug it into the matching end of your car harness.
Plug the other end of the harness back into the gateway. Make sure the connector locks are fully engaged.
Secure the harness box where the trim can fit back in place without pinching any cables.

steps.title: Place mount high and centered on the windshield
body: Clean the mounting area with the included alcohol wipe and let it dry.
Leave enough room for the cable when the device is mounted, and make sure you can see the screen from a seated position.

steps.title: Plug in OBD-C and mount the device
body: Route the long OBD-C cable from the harness box to the windshield. Keep it clear of pedals, moving parts, and airbag deployment paths.
Plug the OBD-C cable into the harness box. Make sure the cable is fully seated.
Plug the OBD-C cable into the comma four. Make sure the cable is all the way in.
Slide the device onto the mount until it is fully seated.

steps.title: Secure the cable and reinstall the trim
body: Secure excess cable so it cannot move into pedals, seat rails, or other moving parts. Keep airbag deployment paths clear.
Check that the harness and cable fit behind the panels, then reinstall the trim you removed.

Volkswagen Arteon 2018-23.title: Volkswagen Arteon
Volkswagen Arteon 2018-23.summary: Your VW J533 connector connects at the gateway. Follow the vehicle-specific steps below.

steps.title: Access the gateway under the dashboard
body: Remove the lower dashboard trim in the driver's footwell to reach the gateway.
Identify the gateway and release its connector locking mechanism before unplugging it.

steps.title: Connect the harness at the gateway
body: Unplug the vehicle connector at the gateway and plug it into the matching end of your car harness.
Plug the other end of the harness back into the gateway. Make sure the connector locks are fully engaged.
Secure the harness box where the trim can fit back in place without pinching any cables.

steps.title: Place mount high and centered on the windshield
body: Clean the mounting area with the included alcohol wipe and let it dry.
Leave enough room for the cable when the device is mounted, and make sure you can see the screen from a seated position.
Center the mount horizontally so the device can properly center in the lane.
Peel off the mount's tape cover. Press firmly in the center, then the edges. Make sure no bubbles form.

steps.title: Plug in OBD-C and mount the device
body: Route the long OBD-C cable from the harness box to the windshield. Keep it clear of pedals, moving parts, and airbag deployment paths.
Plug the OBD-C cable into the harness box. Make sure the cable is fully seated.
Plug the OBD-C cable into the comma four. Make sure the cable is all the way in.
Slide the device onto the mount until it is fully seated.

steps.title: Secure the cable and reinstall the trim
body: Secure excess cable so it cannot move into pedals, seat rails, or other moving parts. Keep airbag deployment paths clear.
Check that the harness and cable fit behind the panels, then reinstall the trim you removed.
